Ashaḥer el El — the yotser piyyuṭ for Shabbat Teshuvah (minhag Polin) by Menaḥem ben Makhir

tei:div.tei:head: Ashaḥer el El — the yotser piyyuṭ for Shabbat Teshuvah (minhag Polin) by Menaḥem ben Makhir

tei:lg.tei:l: As I strive for the Deity all the years of my eras,
the God found far and near, justifying me in my judgments.
Return, Israel, to the Cause! (Hosea 14:2)
Before going up to the high place, to the tribunal for judgment, consider,
understand, and seek from the Book, sit in its shade;
take matters with you and return. (Hosea 14:3)
Great in mercy, tilting towards it, like pecking at our pleas;
it is better for a man to trust in Them then trusting in humanity for our support,
Assyria will not save us. (Hosea 14:4)
Our savior, purifying sin, our souls’ hope from saddening;
clarifying the words of our hope in sustaining me with a noble spirit:
I will heal their backsliding, nobly love them. (Hosea 14:5)
Holy!
Disgrace those warring on Ariel will take;
the Deity will account for Their upright forces persistent as of old:
I will be like dew to Israel, blossoming like a rose. (Hosea 14:6)
Ere the heart is directed up over the thorns and thistles,
the fantasies are false, the seducer dismissed, scraped from the house,
its branches spread out like an olive-tree. (Hosea 14:7)
Ultimately Strong, They strengthen Their devoted ones, desiring to save them,
and They show a path to the repentant to beside Their throne —
let those sitting in Their shade rest! (Hosea 14:8)
Zygote of sanctity’s plants and buds, sprung from the rocks and thorns,
hurrying on meager bread when you rise and settle;
Ephraim, with Me what more need for idols? (Hosea 14:9)
Hoping to justify you and grant you life without destruction,
the Gracious One expressed: “Renew, improve your works hanging on the ten!”
Who is wise and understands this? (Hosea 14:10)
To far and near the Good One>s[am? brings in to apply peace:

tei:l.j:divineName: “Lambs, return to your Parent to unify and praise Them!”
Thus the Cause gave Their voice before Their force. (Joel 2:11)

tei:lg.tei:l: “Insofar as I endeavor to be a speedy witness to those straying from Me,
if they return, I Myself will be a good witness to those that witness Me.
So too now“— declared the Cause — “return to Me!” (Joel 2:12)
Contrite spirit is all the offerings; may the crushed listen to Them!
An honor is Their use of crushed vessels, praised and though highly of.
And tear your hearts and not your clothes and return! (Joel 2:13)
Listening is better than the suet of rams – as said Jeroḥam’s heir –
to fulfill rams your lips, one who confesses and forsakes will be graced.
Who knows, They may return and renege!
Mighty One’s camp, empowering Their powerful strength, will rebuke the straying
between them with words of rebuke, to break them open in regret.
Blow a shofar in Zion, sanctify a fast! (Joel 2:15)
Now They forgive and forget and cover iniquity and shortcoming;
that all betrayals be seen as myrrh, cassia, and aloe.
Gather the people, sanctify the community, (Joel 2:16)
setting the order of repentance and prayer and charity, whose atonement is praiseworthy!
A contrite bowed appearance is like burning suet and sacrificing
between the hall and the altar. (Joel 2:17)
On other festivals, it’s called “offering,” but on the covered day, it’s “doing.” Why?
Those who receive amnesty are created anew, as is proclaimed,
And the Cause was zealous for Their land and had mercy on Their people. (Joel 2:18)
Prominent days of repentance, like the additional sacrifices, are ten.
Entreat Them; The Forgiver will stretch out Their hand to receive us!
And the Cause answered and said, “Here I send.” (Joel 2:19)
Chase away and trample the stumbling-stone from misusing you;
be just until I make it pass, and My spirit will renew your deeds,
My hidden one I move far from you.” (Joel 2:20)
Quarrying and sealing Their foundations, They laid out an eternal string.
Their hooks would not stand until repentance preceded.
Do not fear, land! (Joel 2:21)
Rejoicing in it are the comrades; my foundation will not slip.
Their Shepherd drives off the four wild beasts of the land from my pious ones.
Do not fear, tame beasts of the field! (Joel 2:22)
Shoved down from on on earth, speaking, will awake and sprout from the earth.
Fully in the book of life they will be written and not erased,
and children of Zion, cheer and rejoice! (Joel 2:23)
Their pure ones will again be restored, their comptrollers and legislators reinstated.
Their stomachs filled, their hidden portion given to them as said,
And their threshing-floors will be filled with grain. (Joel 2:24)
The bad years, red years, should be filled out and finished;
his pleasant saying should be made true that we may rejoice with corresponding fertile ones:
“and I will fill for you the years.” (Joel 2:25)
Through the rocks of your hewing and the hills of your conception I will consider you clean and pure.
You will bring food into my house, your first fruits and harvest,
and you will eat food and be sated and praise (Joel 2:26)
the Name, honored and awesome, whose righteousness is like the divine mountains.
May it smell like the smell of the given gift-offerings, like the hearth and the altar;
and you will known that in Israel’s midst (Joel 2:27)
is the Holy!
